rows: Penny size hail was reported along Highway 190.
The thunderstorm wind gust was reported at the intersection of Ranch Road 915 and Ranch Road 1828.
A Sheriff's Deputy reported a roof was taken off of a storage building and a utility pole was snapped in half on the east side of Eldorado.
The large hail damaged vehicle windows.

The public reported wind damage along U.S. Highway 277, south of Eldorado. A roof was removed from a pump house, a flagpole was bent over, and a ten foot section of a barn door was blown inward. There was extensive tree damage as well.
This golfball sized hail broke limbs and sky lights on a home.
The sheriff reported golfball size hail just north of Eldorado.
Strong thunderstorm winds knocked down three power poles along U.S. Highway 277.
This hail fell along U.S. Highway 277 which is approximately 4 miles north of Eldorado.
A National Weather Service Cooperative Observer estimated a wind gust to 80 mph.
Law enforcement reported one power pole, several large branches, and some playground equipment damaged.
A trained spotter estimated a thunderstorm wind gust of 60 mph and reported tree limbs down at the intersection of FM Road 2129 and County Road 100.
There were reports of trees blown down in Eldorado.

An amateur radio operator reported nickel to quarter size hail.

Law Enforcement reported a wet microburst winds of 75 to 85 mph which ripped a metal roof and some siding off a residence and also damaged a roof from a nearby barn. The damaging winds also broke some tree limbs.
There were broken windows in some homes in Eldorado. Also, quarter size hail was reported.
